A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' Bézier adaptation and conditional-diffusion UDA framework, despite retitling and reorganization. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments, generated-image examples, and ablations on BraTS, MM-WHS, and abdominal multi-organ data in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports Top-K label accuracy and feasible GPU batch sizes in Section 5.2.

M1.justification: The core pipeline and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. V2 explicitly specifies per-pixel renormalization after Top-K truncation and confidence collapse, whereas v1 already describes convex aggregation and uses K=2 without specifying that normalization. The unchanged pseudocode leaves uncertainty over whether this changes the procedure or clarifies an existing implementation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate BraTS T2-to-T1/T1CE/FLAIR adaptation and bidirectional MRI/CT adaptation on MM-WHS and abdominal multi-organ data. The new Top-K diagnostic uses the existing T2-to-T1CE scenario.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain CycleGAN, CyCADA, ADVENT, FDA, SIFA, PSIGAN, GenericSSL, FPL+, and Diff-style. FLAIR retains its original comparator set without Diff-style, and the cold-start/style-transfer comparators also remain unchanged. Newly cited diffusion methods are not added to the evaluations.

E3.justification: Reported diffusion training changes from batch size 22 in v1 Appendix G to 7 in v2 Section 9, retaining 250,000 iterations; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. V2 also introduces voxel-level Top-K accuracy evaluation and an H100 batch-capacity analysis. Dataset splits and segmentation-training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the confidence-map analysis with measurements of true-label coverage across ranks and feasible batch sizes, but removes the K=3 downstream segmentation row from Table 7. Component, cold-start, style-transfer, backbone, and hyperparameter analyses otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run variability. The confidence-map calibration metrics already appear in v1; the added Top-K measurements do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds Top-1/2/3/4 accuracies of 0.9783/0.9954/0.9987/1.0000 and maximum batch sizes of 48/24/16 for K=1/2/3. It removes the K=3 Table 7 result with average Dice 53.23 and distance 27.45. All retained tabulated numerical entries match, including relocated 95HD and appendix results.

T1.justification: V2 adds a minimum-MSE aggregation theorem and proof, an excess-risk theorem for surrogate-distribution mismatch, and a Top-K projection/error-bound lemma with derivation in Sections 4 and 7–8. V1 contains diffusion and Bézier formulations but no corresponding theoretical results.

C1.justification: V2 adds minimum-MSE optimality under a surrogate label distribution as a principal contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It recasts the contribution around robust multi-channel diffusion training, with Bézier adaptation supporting pseudo-condition quality, rather than v1's more balanced emphasis on style transfer and diffusion augmentation.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the explanation of aggregation through surrogate-distribution fidelity, mismatch-induced score bias, and Top-K approximation limits. These add applicability qualifications beyond v1's qualitative confidence-weighting rationale. The existing computational limitation is retained and quantified in the Top-K discussion.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code URL and specifies volume-wise min-max normalization for BraTS and abdominal data, plus the source of MM-WHS preprocessing. It revises diffusion batch-size and GPU/CPU/RAM disclosures, distinguishing the H100 capacity analysis from training on three RTX 8000 GPUs. Most implementation and pseudo-labeling details are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially repositions the work around noisy conditioning in existing diffusion-UDA pipelines, adding discussion of Diffuse-UDA, AdaptDiff, ControlUDA, and Noise Optimized Conditional Diffusion, among others. V1 emphasizes limitations of GAN translation more strongly. Several Bézier and histogram-matching references are removed.

P1.justification: The title and framework name change to UPDiff-UDA, and the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Diffusion training precedes Bézier adaptation, much Bézier explanation moves to the supplement, and the appendix is reorganized. Standalone ethics, reproducibility, and broader-impact sections disappear.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1 around prior versus uncertainty-guided diffusion and expands Figure 2 to show downstream augmentation. Main Tables 1–3 are split into Dice tables and supplementary 95HD Tables 8–10; algorithms are stacked instead of side by side. Typography, margins, headers, and table layouts change throughout, while qualitative result imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful explanations, code/preprocessing disclosures, and Top-K diagnostics. However, its new Section 8 claims that any omitted label probability forces positive truncation error, although its projection formula permits zero error when the full mixture lies in the retained score hull. It also removes the K=3 segmentation result and leaves the batch-size revision unexplained despite identical retained scores. These gains and unresolved theoretical and reproducibility issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
